# `ptfkit.williams1992`

```cpp
import ptfkit.williams1992;
```

**Exported namespace:** `ptfkit::williams1992`

Williams et al. (1992) Campbell water-retention regressions and parameter table.

## Source

Williams, J., Ross, P. J., & Bristow, K. L. (1992). Prediction of the Campbell water retention function from texture, structure, and organic matter. In M. Th. van Genuchten, F. J. Leij, & L. J. Lund (Eds.), Proceedings of the International Workshop on Indirect Methods for Estimating the Hydraulic Properties of Unsaturated Soils (pp. 427-441). University of California, Riverside.

## Scope

**Territory:** Australia, England and Wales, and the United States

**Dataset:** Regressions were developed from the Prebble and Forrest Australian data sets, their combination, or the Hall England-and-Wales data set, and were evaluated where compatible against independent Australian, UK, and US data.

[PTF catalog page](../../../ptf-catalog/sources/williams1992.md)

## `SoilStructure`

Source-defined two-level indicator for absence or presence of pedality.

```cpp
enum class SoilStructure {
    Massive,
    Structured,
};
```

| Member | Canonical value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Massive` | `1` | Massive soil, assigned STR = 1. |
| `Structured` | `2` | Structured soil, assigned STR = 2. |

## Functions

### `calc_ptf_williams1992_function_1` {#function-calc_ptf_williams1992_function_1}

Predict volumetric water content with Williams et al. Function 1.

```cpp
[[nodiscard]]
inline double calc_ptf_williams1992_function_1(double clay, double fine_sand, double coarse_sand, double organic_matter, double water_potential)
```

#### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `clay` | Clay below 0.002 mm, as a mass percentage. (%) |
| `fine_sand` | Fine sand from 0.02 to 0.20 mm, as a mass percentage. (%) |
| `coarse_sand` | Coarse sand from 0.20 to 2.0 mm, as a mass percentage. (%) |
| `organic_matter` | Organic-matter mass percentage. (%) |
| `water_potential` | Water-potential magnitude. (bar) |

#### Returns

Predicted volumetric water content at the supplied water-potential magnitude. (%)

!!! note

    Natural logarithms are used.

!!! warning

    The source does not publish exact multivariate calibration boundaries.

### `calc_ptf_williams1992_function_6` {#function-calc_ptf_williams1992_function_6}

Predict volumetric water content with Williams et al. Function 6.

```cpp
[[nodiscard]]
inline double calc_ptf_williams1992_function_6(double clay, double fine_sand, TextureClass texture_class, double organic_matter, double silt, double water_potential)
```

#### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `clay` | Clay below 0.002 mm, as a mass percentage. (%) |
| `fine_sand` | Fine sand from 0.02 to 0.20 mm, as a mass percentage. (%) |
| `texture_class` | Northcote field-texture group supplying TEX in the Function 6 regression. |
| `organic_matter` | Organic-matter mass percentage. (%) |
| `silt` | Silt from 0.002 to 0.02 mm, as a mass percentage. (%) |
| `water_potential` | Water-potential magnitude. (bar) |

#### Returns

Predicted volumetric water content at the supplied water-potential magnitude. (%)

!!! note

    The printed ln(C^2) term is evaluated literally as the natural logarithm of clay squared.

!!! warning

    The source reports collapse for high-clay British Fen soils with organic matter exceeding 30 percent.

!!! warning

    The source does not publish exact multivariate calibration boundaries.
